transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you—please come in and have a seat. What has been bothering you lately that made you decide to come in today?

I’ve been feeling really anxious and worried pretty much all the time, about a lot of different things, and it’s been going on for a long while now. It feels like I can’t switch my mind off, and it’s starting to interfere with my day-to-day life, so I thought I should get some help.
How long have you been feeling this constant anxiety and worry—would you say it’s been more than six months, or less than that?
It’s definitely been more than six months—closer to about a year and eight months now. It’s been pretty constant over that time, without really letting up.

Do you ever have sudden episodes where, out of the blue, you feel an intense surge of fear or discomfort that peaks within a few minutes, along with physical symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, chest pain, or feeling like you might lose control or die?
No, I don’t really get sudden intense attacks like that. For me it’s more of a constant, ongoing anxiety in the background rather than short bursts that peak in a few minutes.
Did your anxiety and constant worrying start after a specific stressful or traumatic event in your life, or did it seem to come on gradually without any clear trigger?
It seemed to come on gradually rather than after one specific event. I can’t really pinpoint a clear trigger—it just felt like over time I started worrying more and more until it became my normal.

Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling mostly down or depressed and losing interest or pleasure in activities you usually enjoy, or is it more that you feel mainly anxious and worried but your mood is otherwise okay?
It’s mainly that I feel anxious and worried all the time, but my mood otherwise is mostly okay. I still enjoy things when I can focus on them; it’s just the constant worry that gets in the way.

Along with the constant worrying, do you often feel physically tense, restless, easily fatigued, have trouble concentrating, feel irritable, or have difficulty falling or staying asleep—and if so, which of these bother you the most?

Yes, I often feel really physically tense, especially in my neck and shoulders, and I catch myself clenching my jaw a lot. My muscles in general feel stiff and achy most of the time, and that constant tension is probably what bothers me the most.
Do you find it very hard to control or stop the worrying once it starts, and is it happening on most days to the point that it interferes with your work, studies, or relationships?

Yeah, once I start worrying it’s really hard to stop—it kind of snowballs and I can’t switch it off, even when I try to distract myself. It’s happening on most days now, and it definitely interferes with my concentration at work and makes it hard to be fully present with people.
Are your worries mainly about everyday things like work, health, family, and finances across different areas of your life, or are they mostly focused on one specific situation or fear?

They’re mostly about everyday things across lots of areas of my life. I worry about work performance and making mistakes, but also about my family’s health, money, and even small day‑to‑day things like whether I’ve forgotten to do something important.

In the past year or so, has there been any major ongoing stressor or life change (like a serious conflict, caregiving burden, or big work or family problem) that directly started and continues to drive your anxiety, or does the anxiety seem more free‑floating and not tied to one particular situation even though life can be stressful at times?

It feels more free‑floating and not tied to one big thing, even though there have definitely been stressful moments with work and money here and there. The anxiety just seems to latch onto whatever is going on at the time rather than coming from one specific ongoing problem.

opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you—please come in and have a seat. What has been bothering you lately that made you decide to come in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports excessive, hard-to-control worry about multiple everyday domains (work, family health, finances, minor daily tasks) occurring on most days for approximately 1 year and 8 months. The anxiety is free‑floating rather than tied to a single stressor, is associated with marked muscle tension and difficulty concentrating, and causes significant functional impairment at work and in relationships. There are no discrete panic attacks, no predominant depressive symptoms, and no single identifiable precipitating stressor or adjustment context, which supports a diagnosis of generalized anxiety disorder (F41.1) over panic disorder or adjustment disorder.
